parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need for pure local ESM .mjs modules under /output, manual process.argv parsing, AES-CBC behavior without node:crypto cipher APIs, Python bytes formatting, and direct executable probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while spawning cli_probe for executable edge cases; cli_probe then spawned aes_probe and also acted as an implementation owner in the same /output workspace.
parallel.implementation: The parent first added lib/aes, lib/cli, lib/format, errors, and /output/test7.mjs; the child later added a second overlapping module layout and a second /output/test7.mjs before the parent repaired the tree.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration was disrupted by competing shared-output files. The parent read the changed entry file, identified another active implementation, deleted the child-owned alternate modules, and recreated the required test7.mjs entrypoint.
parallel.verification: After cleanup the parent ran sample checks, parser edge cases, ambiguous-help cases, negative-value handling, and 16/24/32 byte key checks against the executable before finalizing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The delivered artifact passed only 5 of 28 official samples despite local parity checks; the visible parallel-specific defect is the shared deliverable overwrite and cleanup, not a proven unique cause of the evaluator failures.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same prompt requirements: local .mjs ESM modules, manual argparse-like CLI parsing, exact Python bytes output, direct executable probing, and no external dependencies.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery with multi-agent disabled and no subagents.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote one coherent module tree once, including AES support modules, utf8 formatting, CLI parsing, and /output/test7.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run had no competing writers in /output; its only deliverable placement was the single patch that added the final module tree and entrypoint.
serial.verification: The serial agent verified the first sample, remaining samples, parser edge cases, random valid inputs, repeated options, and bytes repr formatting before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial delivered artifact also passed only 5 of 28 official samples, so the final task correctness problem remained even without parallel shared-state interference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the core requirements: pure Node ESM, .mjs files under /output, manual CLI parity, AES-CBC logic, Python bytes output, no npm modules, and no node:crypto cipher APIs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and recognized the same implementation, CLI, output formatting, and dependency constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements recognition difference is evidenced; both final artifacts targeted the same task obligations and both failed official evaluation at the same score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by spawning cli_probe for CLI edge cases while the parent implemented, but the child also assumed overlapping implementation responsibility in the shared output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial disabled multi-agent execution and kept all probing, implementation, integration, and verification under one owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split created dual implementation ownership over /output/test7.mjs, while serial had one implementation owner and no delegation boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent and child shared enough task context to probe and implement, but there was no effective file ownership boundary preventing both from writing the same entry deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent handoff or cross-agent file interface and therefore no chance for an ownership contract to be violated.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant interface difference was shared workspace ownership, not missing task facts: the parallel child and parent both wrote the entrypoint, whereas the serial run had no cross-agent contract to manage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created an AES, CBC, CLI parser, formatter, runtime-error module set, but this implementation path was interrupted by a child-written alternate implementation and subsequent cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced one AES/CBC/parser/formatter module tree and did not need to replace another actor's code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented comparable AES-CBC and CLI behavior, but parallel had a detour through conflicting module layouts and an entrypoint rewrite that serial avoided.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child result eventually returned and the parent read it, then acted on one parser finding after repairing the overwritten workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all findings stayed in one thread and were applied directly before finalization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not lose the child result, but the result lifecycle intersected with an already-mutated /output tree; serial had no join or handoff step.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent explicitly observed that /output/test7.mjs was no longer its version, found alternate child-created modules in /output, and cleaned and recreated the entry deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run added one /output tree in a single patch and had no shared-output conflict to reconcile.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the central task-solving process difference: parallel suffered a concrete shared deliverable overwrite and recovery step; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After cleanup, parallel ran a normalized parity sweep and several targeted edge cases before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial similarly verified samples, CLI parser cases, repeated options, and bytes repr behavior before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both did substantial local verification and both still failed official evaluation; parallel verification had to occur after a workspace cleanup, while serial verification followed its single implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used three subagents and substantially more token/tool budget, but did not time out and closed after final checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer requests and tools, did not time out, and closed after final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The extra parallel budget was spent partly on overlapping work and reconciliation, but the completed official result remained the same 5 of 28 as serial.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial failed with 5 of 28 samples. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level, not outcome-level: the parallel attempt had competing live writes to the required /output/test7.mjs deliverable and had to audit, delete alternate child files, and recreate the entrypoint before verification, while the serial attempt wrote and verified one coherent tree without shared-state reconciliation.
parallel_contributors: Parallel produced a realized shared-output overwrite and repair episode around /output/test7.mjs.
Parallel still performed post-repair parity checks before finalizing, so the overwrite is not treated as an official outcome-differential cause.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided delegation and shared-write reconciliation by maintaining a single implementation owner.
Serial nevertheless failed the same official test count, so its ordinary implementation limitations remained.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts implemented custom AES-CBC and manual argparse-like behavior but differed in module layout and some local verification routes.
The official 5 of 28 result for both modes indicates unresolved functional coverage not uniquely attributable to the parallel overwrite episode.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process consequence only

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was not absent: both the parent and cli_probe actively produced implementation files, including /output/test7.mjs.
The parent explicitly owned integration after detecting the overwrite and reconciled the output tree, so the defect is a write collision rather than an unowned integration step.
The required entrypoint was assembled and then recreated by the parent; final assembly had an owner even though shared writes disturbed it.
The parent controlled the end-to-end sequence from probing through cleanup, verification, and final response; no pipeline stage was left ownerless.
The parent began implementation while the child probed executable behavior; productive work was not blocked behind one serial preflight gate.
Investigation and implementation overlapped, and the adverse event was the child writing an alternate implementation, not a separate investigation phase that deferred productive work.
The indispensable implementation path was active in both parent and child; the concrete adverse consequence was conflicting writes, not under-allocation to the critical path.

Although multiple subagents ran, the run did not time out and completed final verification; there is no direct evidence that fan-out collectively exhausted the budget before required work could finish.
cli_probe completed and returned findings, and its issue was overstepping into shared implementation files rather than failing an overbroad assigned scope.
No parent-known task, environment, acceptance, or delivery requirement is shown as omitted from a child brief and causing unusable work; the observed harm is the child writing the shared deliverable.

The competing work involved a direct replacement of the entry deliverable in the shared workspace, which the taxonomy classifies under concurrent writes rather than an abstract missing interface contract.
There is no evidence that known information disappeared during transfer; the parent received child results and the observed problem was a file overwrite.
The child final report was available and concise enough for the parent to act on; no required action was left unfinished because a handoff was too large to reduce.
The parent did not proceed from stale child information; it observed the current filesystem state and reconciled the changed output tree before final checks.
There were competing implementations, but they manifested as concrete shared-file writes and were adjudicated by cleanup; no incompatible reports remained unadjudicated at closure.
The parent did not accept the whole task solely on file existence or workflow return; it ran post-cleanup parity checks before finalizing, and evaluator failure alone cannot establish this label.
No replacement or retry was launched without inherited findings; the child returned and the parent continued in the same run.

The parent performed final parity checks after the cleanup and entrypoint rewrite, so the shared-state repair was not merely merged after verification without a closing check.
The child implementation was not silently unjoined; it entered the shared workspace directly and the parent later inspected and reconciled it.
The nested probe produced findings and the cli_probe final answer was returned to the parent; no verifier finding was trapped below the parent before closure.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled with unfinished scope that the parent ignored; the parent instead took over the conflicting workspace state.
The parent saw the cli_probe result and acted on its parser finding; no visible completed result was ignored while proceeding inconsistently with it.
The parent actively inspected files and agent state; an invalid short wait attempt and normal waits did not constitute waiting until deadline without inspection.
Competing module layouts existed, but the same episode includes a proven entry deliverable replacement, so Deliverable Overwrite is the more specific retained label.
Two agents edited the same file, but that file was the required executed entry deliverable; the taxonomy gives Deliverable Overwrite precedence.
The decisive overwrite involved /output/test7.mjs, the required entrypoint deliverable, not only a non-entry library or configuration source file.
